subject: Cognitive Science
title: Wisdom of Crowds
description: A quick, practical guide to Wisdom of Crowds.

hook.text: At a county fair in 1906, 800 people guessed the weight of an ox. The average guess was off by one pound.

buildup.text: Francis Galton was stunned. No individual was accurate, but the crowd's average was nearly perfect.

discovery.text: Crowd wisdom works when opinions are diverse, independent, and aggregated. Individual errors cancel out.

twist.text: But if people see each other's guesses, independence breaks. Social influence destroys crowd wisdom.

climax.text: Prediction markets work on this principle: aggregate independent bets and you get remarkably accurate forecasts.

punchline.text: A crowd of independent thinkers beats any single expert.

quiz.question: What condition is essential for crowd wisdom to work?
